question: Which of the following molecular formulas belongs to cyclic hydrocarbons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**(C6H12)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **C₆H₁₂** is the molecular formula for a cyclohexane, which is a cyclic hydrocarbon.
 
• Cyclic hydrocarbons are compounds that contain a hydrocarbon ring.
 
• C₆H₁₂ follows the general formula of cycloalkanes, which is **CₙH₂ₙ** where n is the number of carbon atoms in the ring.
 
• Cyclohexane is a saturated hydrocarbon, meaning it only has single bonds between carbon atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cyclic Hydrocarbons**

 
 
• Cyclic hydrocarbons are organic compounds that consist of carbon atoms arranged in a ring or cycle.
 
• They can be either saturated (cycloalkanes) or unsaturated (cycloalkenes, cycloalkynes).
 
• Cycloalkanes have the general formula **CₙH₂ₙ** and contain only single bonds.
 
• Cycloalkenes and cycloalkynes contain double and triple bonds, respectively, and have different general formulas.
 
 
 
• **Other Options**
 
 
• **(C₅H₁₂)**: This is the molecular formula for pentane, which is an acyclic (straight-chain) hydrocarbon.
 
• **(C₄H₁₀)**: This is the molecular formula for butane, another acyclic hydrocarbon.
 
• **(C₇H₁₆)**: This is the molecular formula for heptane, which is also an acyclic hydrocarbon.
